We mark each cable before unplugging it because once it's loose, nothing on the cable itself tells you where it goes. The mark records which socket it belongs in, so whoever plugs it back in, maybe hours later or someone else entirely, puts it in the right place instead of guessing.

We keep the marks on until after everything is reconnected because they are also how we check our work. Once the cables are back in, we compare each one against its mark. If a cable sits in a socket that doesn't match its label, two have been swapped, and we catch it then rather than when the wrong light, speaker or feed comes up during the show. If we pulled the marks as we plugged in, there would be nothing left to check against.
